QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_8

question.text: Per Table 4.4 in the chapter, which parameter most sharply differentiates a Specialised Investment Fund (SIF) from a Category III AIF?

answer.text: Minimum investment amount — SIF is INR 10 lakh across all strategies of the AMC; Cat III AIF is INR 1 crore
Issue process — SIF uses private placement; Cat III AIF uses public issue
Investor cap — SIF is capped at 1,000 investors; Cat III AIF has no cap
Sponsor commitment — SIF requires 5% of corpus or INR 10 crore; Cat III AIF has no such requirement

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 4.4: SIF minimum investment is INR 10 lakh across ALL strategies of the AMC; Cat III AIF minimum is INR 1 crore. SIF uses public issue (same as MF parent); Cat III uses private placement. SIF has no investor cap; Cat III capped at 1,000. Sponsor commits: SIF sponsor has a track record + AUM test; Cat III sponsor/manager holds 5%/INR 10 cr whichever lower. The Trap: Option B inverts the issue process. Option C inverts investor caps. Option D wrongly says Cat III has no sponsor commitment — it does. Cross-Exam Context: SIF is a 2024-25 SEBI-introduced structure. XIX-C now tests it vs MF and AIF. XIX-E focuses the Cat III-vs-SIF cut. SIFs democratise some Cat III-like strategies at a lower ticket but lose the private-placement + leverage freedom. Manager's Pro-Tip: When a prospect says 'I only have INR 25 lakh — can I get a long-short strategy?', the answer is an SIF from a large AMC (INR 10 lakh minimum), not your Cat III AIF. Cat III remains the INR 1 crore+ UHNI/institutional product.
